blocks.text: Selling a home is more than the sale price. The mortgage payout, commission, legal fees and other costs all come off before you receive anything. This calculator adds up what you tell it and shows what you would be left with. The figures come from you: your listing agreement, your lender’s payout statement and your lawyer’s or notary’s estimate.

FAQ for home sellers in BC

blocks.text: It does not include income tax or capital gains tax. A home that has been your principal residence is often exempt from capital gains tax, but that depends on your situation, so ask an accountant. It also does not model a purchase that completes on a different date from your sale, bridge financing, a seller credit to the buyer or a price that changes after offers. Treat the result as a planning number and ask Jared to walk through it with the real figures once you are ready to list.

faq.q: How much will I walk away with after selling my home?
faq.a: Take the sale price and subtract your mortgage payout, the commission and any tax on it, legal or notary fees, any prepayment penalty, the adjustments you owe and other costs of selling. The calculator above does that with the figures you enter.

faq.q: What commission rate does the calculator use?
faq.a: None. Commission is negotiable and set in your listing agreement, so you type in the percentage that applies to you. The calculator has no built-in rates.

faq.q: Are my numbers saved or sent anywhere?
faq.a: No. The calculation runs in your browser, and nothing you type is sent to Jared or stored.

faq.q: Does the estimate include income tax or capital gains tax?
faq.a: No. Whether tax applies depends on your situation, for example whether the home was your principal residence, so ask an accountant.

faq.q: Can Jared give me a number for my own home?
faq.a: Yes. Jared can review comparable sales for your address and go through the costs with you. Start with the free home evaluation.
